Alloys with the equiatomic compositions of CoCrFeMnNi HEA were produced by arc melting of pure elements (99.9% purity) under argon atmosphere. Ingots were flipped and completely remelted at least five times to ensure its chemical composition homogeneity.
The rectangular specimens with a size of 100 mm × 20 mm × 10 mm were prepared by Cu molds drop casting method.
The homogenization of the rectangular specimens was carried out at 1473 K for 24 h under the vacuum argon atmosphere, and then air-cooled to room temperature.

other.pre_soak: at least 20 min in liquid nitrogen before each pass

evidence.quote: To ensure cryo-deformation between the rolling passes, the specimens were submerged in liquid nitrogen at least 20min before each rolling pass. A thickness reduction ~90% was finally performed after 20 rolling passes
and followed by annealing at 923 K for 30 min and 1073 K for 60 min for recrystallization, respectively.

mechanisms.name: deformation twinning
mechanisms.material_state: UFG after annealing at 923 K for 30 min, tensile tested at 77 K

evidence.quote: The superior combination of the strength-ductility for the Cantor alloy at 77 K is attributed to the deformation twinning.

mechanisms.name: grain boundary relaxation
mechanisms.material_state: UFG after annealing at 923 K for 30 min

evidence.quote: The UFG alloy exhibited plastic instability and was prominently strengthened with increasing testing temperature from 293 K to 473 K, which was related to obviously grain boundaries relaxation in HEAs.

mechanisms.name: dynamic Hall-Petch effect
mechanisms.material_state: UFG after annealing at 923 K for 30 min

evidence.quote: newly formed twin boundaries firstly act as a coherent and stable interface strongly obstructing the dislocation movement, secondly cause continuous grain fragmentation, which reduces the mean free path of dislocation glide and causes dynamic Hall-Petch effect
